# Agents working on Pepper Row ordering

This repository is maintained mostly by coding agents. A human (the head of engineering for the Pepper Row group) reviews every pull request. Read this file before you change anything.

## The system

- `api/`: the ordering API (Python 3.12, FastAPI, asyncpg). Menu, orders, the allergen check, ticket routing, payment handoff to Tillpoint.
- `kds/`: the kitchen display (TypeScript, Vite, no framework). One screen per station.
- `db/migrations/`: Postgres schema. Append only; never edit a migration that has shipped.
- `docs/`: the allergen policy and the order lifecycle. They are the specification.

## Who does what

Three subagents live in `.claude/agents/`. Delegate to the one whose remit covers the change; do not do their work in the main session.

| Agent | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `menu-curator` | menu items, sections, 86'ing dishes |
| `order-flow-engineer` | the order lifecycle, kitchen tickets, the payment handoff, the kitchen display |
| `allergen-auditor` | the allergen rule, its tests and the allergen banner; reviews every change that touches allergen data |

## Rules for every agent

1. Run `make test` before you open a pull request.
2. The allergen rule in `docs/allergen-policy.md` is not negotiable. If a change would weaken it, stop and ask.
3. Never handle card data. The API creates payment intents; the processor does the rest.
4. Migrations are append only.

## GlossMark vocabulary

Link what you write to the ontology with one comment line per declaration, in the file's own comment syntax:

```
@gloss[?] <relation> <target>[, <target>...] [scope=file|symbol|block|line|range] [conf=0.0-1.0] [note="..."]
```

- Write `@gloss?` for links you are proposing; a human accepts them with `gloss accept`. Never write a bare `@gloss` for a link you are not sure of.
- If no concept fits, write `@gloss? <relation> <ns>:NEW:<Name> note="why"`, then run `gloss propose --from-new --doc "what it is"` (MCP: propose_concept) so the concept ships in the same PR with `proposed: true`; a human accepts it with `gloss accept --concept <ns>:<Name>`. Never invent a concept name any other way, and never hand-edit an ontology file to make a link resolve.
- Relations you may use inline: `configures`, `consumes`, `deploys`, `documents`, `hosts`, `implements`, `instructs`, `may-modify`, `presents`, `produces`, `provisions`, `publishes`, `publishes-value`, `represents`, `subscribes`, `tests`, `verifies`. Use `implements` for behaviour, `represents` for data shapes, `verifies` in tests, `provisions`/`configures`/`deploys` in IaC, config and CI.

### Concepts

**dine:** (core)

| Concept | Kind | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dine:Allergen` | entity | One of the fourteen allergens UK food law requires a restaurant to declare. |
| `dine:AllergenRule` | constraint | No dish containing, or possibly containing, a guest's declared allergen is fired without staff acknowledgement, and every ticket carrying it is flagged at its station. |
| `dine:Checkout` | process | Taking payment for a served order. |
| `dine:KitchenFulfilment` | process | Cooking a fired order station by station until every ticket is bumped. |
| `dine:KitchenTicket` | entity | The part of an order one kitchen station cooks, shown on that station's screen. |
| `dine:Location` | entity | One Pepper Row restaurant: Canal Street, Harbour or Market Hall. |
| `dine:Menu` | entity | What one location offers tonight, grouped into sections. |
| `dine:MenuItem` | entity | One dish with its price, its station and the allergens it contains or may contain. |
| `dine:MenuPublishing` | process | Deciding what a location offers and in which sections, and taking a dish off when the kitchen runs out. |
| `dine:Order` | entity | What one table asked for, with the allergens the guests declared. |
| `dine:Ordering` | process | Opening an order for a table and firing it to the kitchen. |
| `dine:Payment` | entity | Money taken for an order through the card processor, tip included. |
| `dine:Station` | entity | A section of the kitchen line: grill, fry, saute, cold, pastry or the pass. |

**pepper:** (implementation)

| Concept | Kind | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pepper:AllergenBanner` | process | Pins every open ticket with an allergen alert to the top of the station screen. |
| `pepper:AllergenGuard` | process | find_conflicts and enforce_allergen_rule: refuses to fire an unacknowledged conflict and returns what tickets must flag.; realizes dine:AllergenRule |
| `pepper:KitchenDisplay` | system-type | The TypeScript kitchen display: one screen per station.; realizes dine:KitchenFulfilment |
| `pepper:MenuAvailability` | process | Taking a dish off a location's menu for the rest of service when the kitchen runs out, and restoring it. |
| `pepper:MenuCatalog` | process | Groups a location's available items into sections in service order; 86's and restores items.; realizes dine:MenuPublishing |
| `pepper:OrderFlow` | process | The order state machine: open, fire, serve, void.; realizes dine:Ordering |
| `pepper:OrderingApi` | system-type | The FastAPI ordering service: menu, orders, the allergen check, ticket routing and the payment handoff.; realizes dine:Checkout; realizes dine:MenuPublishing; realizes dine:Ordering |
| `pepper:PaymentHandoff` | process | Creates a Tillpoint payment intent and settles the order from the signed webhook; never sees card data.; realizes dine:Checkout |
| `pepper:TicketBoard` | process | The station screen: one card per open ticket, late tickets highlighted, a bump button. |
| `pepper:TicketRouter` | process | Splits a fired order into one ticket per station, with the allergen alert on the stations that cook a flagged dish.; realizes dine:KitchenFulfilment |
| `pepper:TicketStore` | process | Client-side state: the open tickets of one station, oldest first. |

<!-- gloss:end -->
